async ({ replaceIn }) => {
  const res = [];
  res.push(await replaceIn({ file: "README.md", pairs: [
    [`- **Your conventions.** pi follows the conventions of your repository: its git hooks, \`AGENTS.md\`, and \`CONTRIBUTING.md\`. pi-action installs no git hooks of its own. See [Commit conventions](docs/how-it-works.md#commit-conventions).`,
     `- **Your conventions.** pi-action puts your \`AGENTS.md\` (or \`CLAUDE.md\`) into the system prompt, as pi does, so your rules apply from the first request. pi follows your git hooks, and installs none of its own. See [The system prompt](docs/prompts.md#the-system-prompt) and [Commit conventions](docs/how-it-works.md#commit-conventions).`],
    [`| \`exclude_tools\` |`, `| \`context_files\` | Put \`AGENTS.md\` (or \`CLAUDE.md\`) into the system prompt: the one in \`agent_dir\`, then one for each directory from the workspace root down to the working directory. On a pull request from a fork, they come from its base commit (see [The system prompt](docs/prompts.md#the-system-prompt)) | No | \`true\` |
| \`context_files_max_bytes\` | Maximum size of all context files together, in bytes. pi-action cuts a file at the limit, tells the model, and writes a warning | No | \`65536\` |
| \`exclude_tools\` |`],
  ]}));
  res.push(await replaceIn({ file: "docs/how-it-works.md", pairs: [
    [`4. **Load models and extensions** ([\`src/models.ts\`](../src/models.ts), [\`src/extensions.ts\`](../src/extensions.ts)). See [Models](models.md) and [Extensions](extensions.md).`,
     `4. **Load models, extensions, and context files** ([\`src/models.ts\`](../src/models.ts), [\`src/extensions.ts\`](../src/extensions.ts), [\`src/context-files.ts\`](../src/context-files.ts)). See [Models](models.md), [Extensions](extensions.md), and [The system prompt](prompts.md#the-system-prompt). pi-action reads \`AGENTS.md\` one time for each run.`],
    [`- Write your commit format in \`AGENTS.md\` or \`CONTRIBUTING.md\`. pi reads these files with its tools, as it reads the rest of your repository. pi-action does not add them to the prompt.`,
     `- Write your commit format in \`AGENTS.md\`. pi-action puts it into the system prompt (see [The system prompt](prompts.md#the-system-prompt)). pi reads other files, such as \`CONTRIBUTING.md\`, with its tools; link to them from \`AGENTS.md\`.`],
  ]}));
  res.push(await replaceIn({ file: "docs/prompts.md", pairs: [
    [`\n## The task\n`, `
## The system prompt

The system prompt has these sections, in this sequence:

1. \`project_context\`: the context files of the repository, from the built-in \`pi-action-context\` extension. Set \`context_files: false\` to remove it.
2. The sections of the pi-durable extensions, in the order of \`extensions\` (for example pit's guidelines). See [Extensions](extensions.md#pi-durable-extensions).

Without context files and extensions, the system prompt is empty.

### Context files

pi-action loads context files as pi's coding agent does:

1. **Global:** \`<agent_dir>/AGENTS.md\`, or else \`<agent_dir>/CLAUDE.md\`. Only when \`agent_dir\` is set.
2. **Workspace:** for each directory from the workspace root (\`GITHUB_WORKSPACE\`) down to the working directory of the agent: \`AGENTS.md\`, or else \`CLAUDE.md\`. Today, the working directory is the workspace root. pi-action never reads files above the workspace.
3. **Nested files** below the working directory (for example \`packages/api/AGENTS.md\`) are not loaded. The section lists their paths (up to 20) and tells pi to read the one for the directory where it works. pi-action finds them with \`git ls-files\`, so it ignores the files that git ignores.

The section looks like this:

\`\`\`text
<project_context>
# Project Context

Project-specific instructions and guidelines:

## /home/runner/work/xyz/xyz/AGENTS.md

<file contents>

More context files: packages/api/AGENTS.md. Read the one for the directory you work in.
</project_context>
\`\`\`

- **Size.** \`context_files_max_bytes\` (default 64 KiB) limits all files together. pi-action cuts the file at the limit, adds a note for pi, leaves out later files, and writes a warning to the log.
- **Text.** pi-action removes invisible characters, as for the issue body (see [Security](security.md#what-pi-action-removes-from-text)). It keeps HTML comments.
- **One read for each run.** pi-action reads the files when the run starts. If pi changes \`AGENTS.md\` during the run, the system prompt stays the same, and the prompt cache of the provider stays valid. The next run on the thread sends the new content as an update of the section.
- **Pull requests from forks.** pi-action reads the files from the base commit of the pull request, not from the checkout. See [Security](security.md#context-files-from-the-repository).
- **The log.** The setup group shows the files, for example \`Context files: AGENTS.md (2.1 KiB)\`.

## The task
`],
  ]}));
  res.push(await replaceIn({ file: "docs/security.md", pairs: [
    [`\n## Thread contents are visible\n`, `
## Context files from the repository

\`AGENTS.md\` and \`CLAUDE.md\` go into the system prompt (see [Context files](prompts.md#context-files)). The system prompt has more weight for the model than a file that it reads. pi-action reads these files from the checkout, so their content is the content of the checked-out ref:

- **Pull requests from forks** (\`pull_request\` events whose head is in another repository): pi-action reads the files from the base commit of the pull request (\`pull_request.base.sha\`), and fetches it if the clone does not have it. If it cannot read the base commit, it loads no workspace files and writes a warning. The author of the fork cannot change the system prompt.
- **Pull requests from branches of the same repository:** pi-action uses the \`AGENTS.md\` of the branch. People who can push a branch can already change the code that your workflow runs.
- pi-action removes invisible characters from the files, but keeps HTML comments, because \`AGENTS.md\` files use them.
- Set \`context_files: false\` to load no files.

## Thread contents are visible
`],
  ]}));
  res.push(await replaceIn({ file: "docs/extensions.md", pairs: [
    [`The order is: the coding tools of pi-action (\`coding-tools\`) first, then the extensions in the order of the \`extensions\` input.`,
     `The order is: the coding tools of pi-action (\`coding-tools\`) first, then pi-action's \`pi-action-context\` (the \`project_context\` section, see [The system prompt](prompts.md#the-system-prompt)), then the extensions in the order of the \`extensions\` input. Extensions cannot use the names \`coding-tools\` and \`pi-action-context\`.`],
  ]}));
  res.push(await replaceIn({ file: "CONTRIBUTING.md", pairs: [
    [`| [\`src/durable-extensions.ts\`](src/durable-extensions.ts) |`, `| [\`src/context-files.ts\`](src/context-files.ts) | The context files (\`AGENTS.md\`, \`CLAUDE.md\`) and the built-in \`pi-action-context\` extension with the \`project_context\` section |
| [\`src/durable-extensions.ts\`](src/durable-extensions.ts) |`],
  ]}));
  return res.length;
}
